dateRangePicker.$description: A date-range picker — the date window of the threads console's filter bar (staff Message Center). One bordered field, `‹ | [calendar icon + 'Aug 08, 2026 – Sep 08, 2026'] | ›`: the middle segment opens the calendar, the arrows step the WHOLE window back/forward by a month (the common case — 'last month', 'the month before' — is one click, no calendar). The panel is a dual-month calendar (two consecutive months side by side, each with month + year selects so a far-off window is two picks instead of a dozen arrow clicks), with Reset (back to the default window) and Apply in the footer; nothing filters until Apply, so a half-picked range never reloads the console. A `--single` one-month variant is for narrow containers (the mobile/tablet filters drawer); the dual panel stacks its months under 560px. Replaces the earlier ‹ start · period label · end › navigator, whose 'Current' label and two separate date fields cost width the console toolbar doesn't have. The calendar inside is the shared Calendar component (calendar.tokens.json, mode range, two months) — header, grid, range band and month gap live there; this file owns only the field, the popover panel and the footer.

height.$description: 40px = the base field height, so it lines up with the Selects/Search beside it in the console toolbar.

bg.$description: The locked-in field recipe: surface.dim fill, hairline border → strong on hover → focus blue.

divider.$description: Hairline between the prev arrow, the range field and the next arrow.

arrowWidth.$description: 32px-wide arrow segment (full field height) — the same 32 as the panel's paging arrows (header.navSize).

paddingX.$description: Inline padding of the middle range field.

value.$description: The range text, 'Mmm DD, YYYY – Mmm DD, YYYY'.

padding.$description: 16px — two months plus a footer is a bigger surface than the single DatePicker's 12px panel.

footer.$description: Reset (left) and Apply (right). Both ARE Buttons — Reset = Button secondary sm, Apply = Button primary sm — so their size and colours come from button.tokens.json, not from this file.
